Both validators read a text twice, as written and as read (normalised with unicode-tables.json), and
every refusal rule but 'quoted' runs on both, so the normalisation can only add refusals. See the
No pattern uses \b, \d, \s, \w or another shorthand .NET's Regex and Python's re read differently.
%word%, %digit%, %space% and %nonspace% are classes written out from unicode-tables.json, which are
what .NET reads as \b's word characters, \d, \s and \S. The 'placeholders' below are built from
them. The rules named in 'ignore_case' ignore case: RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | CultureInvariant in
.NET and re.IGNORECASE | re.ASCII in Python, which agree once U+212A is read as K.
'directive' is production's instruction rule from before ST-061 (DraftValidator.cs at main b989436)
with each shorthand written out, and nothing else changed. Which instruction-shaped sentences are
refused is deliberately not changed here; that is a separate redesign (T-204).
Credentials are refused by shape only (the owner's option A, 2026-10-24): 'secret_shaped' after a
'credential_cue', 'key_shapes', 'key_cue_value', cards and SSNs. A plain word after a cue is not.
